desc:
Given an array nums of non-negative integers, arrange them in some order and glue their decimal representations together to form one big number. Return the largest number that can be formed, as a string.

The result can be far too large for any integer type, hence the string. If the array contains only zeros, return "0" (not "000").

Example: [3, 30, 34, 5, 9] gives "9534330". Example: [10, 2] gives "210".
hints: Sorting the numbers in descending order does not work: [3, 30] must give "330", while "303" is smaller.
For two numbers x and y, only two orders exist: x then y, or y then x. Compare the two concatenated strings x+y and y+x.
Sort with the rule "x comes before y if x+y > y+x as strings". This rule is transitive, so a sort works. Join the result; if the first character is '0', the answer is "0".
editorial: Two numbers a and b should appear as ab when the string a+b is larger than b+a. Both concatenations have the same length, so comparing them as text is the same as comparing them as numbers. This defines a total preorder on the numbers (it is transitive), and an exchange argument shows that sorting by it is optimal: if two neighbours were in the wrong order, swapping them would produce a larger number without touching anything else.

Sort the decimal strings with a comparator based on that rule, join them, and handle the all-zero case by returning "0" when the first character of the joined string is '0' (the maximum arrangement starts with 0 only if every number is 0). Sorting costs O(n log n) comparisons of strings of length up to 20.
solution:
from functools import cmp_to_key


def largestNumber(nums):
    words = [str(x) for x in nums]
    words.sort(key=cmp_to_key(lambda x, y: -1 if x + y > y + x else (1 if x + y < y + x else 0)))
    res = "".join(words)
    return "0" if res[0] == "0" else res
